question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable AI-safety event store and a public plugin emission capability, or should this remain a narrower diagnostics/plugin extension until a stable contract is approved?
rationale: The branch changes core persistence, Gateway/API surface, operator UI, exporters, and the plugin SDK boundary; code review cannot safely choose the long-term ownership and privacy contract.

options.title: Approve a staged core contract
options.body: Approve a minimal documented event schema, retention/privacy policy, and plugin compatibility plan, then split this branch into independently reviewable core and exporter/UI changes.

options.title: Keep it plugin-scoped
options.body: Retain only generic diagnostics seams in core and move safety-specific emitters, storage, dashboards, and exporter behavior into plugins.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or pause this implementation branch while the canonical issue collects an owner-approved product and security design.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a minimal documented event schema, retention/privacy policy, and plugin compatibility plan, then split this branch into independently reviewable core and exporter/UI changes.

likelyOwner.reason: A repository-level product owner is needed because the decision spans core architecture, persisted user data, public plugin APIs, and security-adjacent telemetry.
